problems.symptom: One orphan gap drew 13 drafts in 2 days with contradictory directions (add, delete, make-real) and byte-identical duplicates; nothing converged.
problems.root_cause: Failed drafts left no reason for the next draft to read, so each attempt restarted blind. This is the same class as the 09-22 'failure side had no store' finding.

problems.symptom: orphaned-capability-goal_summary and orphaned-capability-interface_deploy_reach_check are open with first_detected 2026-09-26, reopen_count 0, and falsifier 'none', although the same ids were worked on 2026-08-17.
problems.root_cause: Gap store history was reset or re-created, so recurrence is invisible to the durability metric; orphan gaps carry no machine-checkable close predicate.

problems.symptom: goal_summary producer was minted (dc18b62) to close a missing-shape gap and has never been invoked. The follow-up fix drafts proposed more placeholder resolvers returning constant resolved:true.
problems.root_cause: Gap closure was keyed on 'a producer exists' rather than on the capability being consumed.

problems.symptom: Drafts invent packages and APIs, doubled paths, and literal placeholder comments; they replace 800-line files with 7-line ones and hardcode fake metrics; five ad-hoc edit-spec schemas.
problems.root_cause: The drafter had no contract for its output format and no real file or API context at draft time (information starvation, law 8).

problems.symptom: Draft payloads and tsc .js/.d.ts/.map emit accumulate in openspec/changes: 77 stray files, 60 compiled files, 20 goal_summary entries.
problems.root_cause: Drafts are written into the wrong directory; a tsc run emitted into the super-repo; autonomous drift-sweep commits (4e4170a8, 796fac89) commit the whole tree; the pre-commit gate only checks top-level dirs.

problems.symptom: Pathways that reached but produced inert or reverted changes keep reach-time credit, e.g. registryFieldFor rewritten 8x, each rewrite re-banking credit; confabulated blob 4eedb4de scored CORRECT.
problems.root_cause: Credit is banked at reach time by a surface-plausibility oracle; goal_verification_labels (14,100 rows) is never read by posterior-update.ts; the A/B supersede decision is unsettled.

problems.symptom: Detector finds orphans reliably but no bridge or retire action lands; goal_summary and interface_deploy_reach_check are still at 0 invocations 40+ days later.
problems.root_cause: repair_direction offers only rewire or mint, never retire. For a resolver that was itself a hollow mint, minting a bridge compounds the wrong mint (law 3).

problems.symptom: The live goal_summary resolver hardcodes the fallback process.env.ACTIVITY_API_ENDPOINT ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:8080' and a similar one for the dev-vessel endpoint.
problems.root_cause: The substrate-authored resolver pins ports instead of routing through discovery.

principles: The substrate expresses the full capability surface it advertises; an advertised-but-unexpressed resolver is a gap. (orphaned-capability-scan.ts header / gap cite_principle)
Prefer the deterministic resolver over an llm_completion_dispatch re-derivation. (orphan gap suggested_remediation)
Let what actually happened correct what the oracle guessed: reward must be revisable along the temporal axis (stayed / exercised / reverted / recurred). (2026-08-26-consequence-verdict-into-credit)
Consequence correction is keyed, never heuristic: it attaches to an execution_id or commit, or it does not write (law 12). (same proposal)
Asymmetric caution: reverts and keyed recurrence are confident negatives; not-yet-exercised is absence of evidence and abstains. (same proposal)
No double-count and no second credit system: the existing cascade is the carrier (precedent: decision_outcome kept read-only, 03e6c55). (same proposal)
Settle open design decisions in the spec; do not anchor them in code first. (same proposal)

Tension surfaced by this shard: 'express every advertised capability' vs law 3 'a wrong mint is negative value'. The orphan detector needs a retire direction for resolvers that were themselves hollow mints.
